behaviors: Read the complete legacy source and every facade regression assertion. Configured legacy endpoints are rechecked for every preparation without cached failures, using public health without bearer/query and exact HTTP 200, service/listener/hub identity, connection and catalog readiness. Healthy/down/recovered launches mint exactly twice; non-200 success and redirects refuse before token writes.

Real SessionFacade prepares managed query credentials and private Claude MCP files with Authorization headers, retains selected library servers and strict MCP configuration, replaces only existing t query values, and keeps Claude argv free of bearer bytes. Atomic token mutations preserve unrelated pairings and the prior generation cannot revoke its successor.

Manager preparation preserves operator scope, wildcard plugin compatibility and manager role while omitting obsolete profilesAllowed/yoloAllowed grants. Full-access remains a provider execution preference. Worker escalation contracts survive managed and PTY preparation, both profile prompt spellings compose into one ordered flag, and accidental manager parent metadata does not attach worker escalation.

Real lifecycle and persistent SessionFacade integration verifies credentials exist before both managed/PTY engine calls, failure revokes them, a token-store filesystem failure retains pending cleanup, a repeated stop retries successfully, and later duplicates do not touch the store. Existing lifecycle tests additionally fence old generations and reconcile authoritative stopped rows.

Existing collaboration tests verify exact bundled skill bytes, pointer-only ordinary instructions, manager exclusion and safe refusal without overwriting user content. No old grant enforcement is reinstated.
intentionalChanges: A configured but unverified facade refuses the launch before minting; the old Go path silently omitted tools and continued. Deliberately Disabled remains a supported no-facade launch with selected library MCP and worker contracts. This distinction is documented in mcp-tool-facade context.
Owned Rust readiness uses its in-process actor, exact bound endpoint and launchReady capability proof, rather than trusting a public HTTP responder. Legacy compatibility checks remain separate.

Credential mutation is protected across processes with an advisory lock and durable generation-scoped lifecycle cleanup, replacing the Go process mutex and in-memory stop callback. Session IDs additionally require a portable ASCII filename vocabulary.

Library resolution and collaboration skill responsibilities are reviewed with their owning groups; source-local shim reconcileManagerGrants remains an intentional no-op because obsolete grants are parseable metadata only.

The shared manager doctrine explains how to read worker escalation results; unlike the older short manager prompt, it legitimately names wks-escalation. The regression excludes the actual STRUCTURED WORKER ESCALATION CONTRACT, not every mention of that result format.

Existing unchanged agent_lifecycle, launch_instructions and spawn_plan source/test bytes verified against a7e11447; actual Linux CI run36637635273/job109642057174 passed their owning targets (including generation retry/fencing, authoritative stop reconciliation, exact skill bytes and worker contract). Log /tmp/workspacer-facade-baseline-ci.log. Witness left Rust integration unmapped; explicit owning target supplied current proof. The shared library run separately failed/hung unrelated fixtures and is not claimed green.
